title: Large-Bore Mechanical Thrombectomy Versus Catheter-Directed Thrombolysis in the Management of Intermediate-Risk Pulmonary Embolism: Primary Results of the PEERLESS Randomized Controlled Trial
summary: Among 550 treated patients with intermediate-risk PE already selected for intervention, FlowTriever thrombectomy beat catheter-directed thrombolysis on a hierarchical composite dominated by ICU use (win ratio 5.01, 95% CI 3.68–6.97). Deterioration/bailout occurred in 1.8% versus 5.4%; major bleeding was 6.9% in both groups. Removing ICU utilization eliminated statistical significance (win ratio 1.34, 95% CI 0.78–2.35); mortality benefit was not established.
population: Adults with intermediate-risk proximal PE, RV dysfunction and additional clinical risk.
shortTitle: PEERLESS: choosing between catheter treatments for intermediate-risk PE
limitations: Open-label, manufacturer-sponsored trial with protocol-sensitive ICU outcomes, variable thrombolysis regimens and 49 postrandomization exclusions. Bleeding-risk selection and short follow-up limit generalization.
whyItMatters: This informs PERT discussions after deciding on catheter treatment. It cannot establish that intervention improves outcomes over anticoagulation alone.
evidenceNotes:
Main methods, results, harms and limitations reviewed; supplements not independently reviewed. PubMed corroborates October 29 electronic publication. Bounded DOI correction/retraction search found no separate notice, without exhaustive assurance.

Later HI-PEITHO and PRAGUE-26 compared catheter thrombolysis with anticoagulation, addressing a different question; their primary abstracts were checked: https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2516567 and https://doi.org/10.1056/NEJMoa2608012 . They do not establish mechanical-thrombectomy superiority over medical care.
primaryEndpoint: Hierarchical death, intracranial hemorrhage, major bleeding, deterioration/bailout and ICU utilization through discharge/day 7.
